evidence.block_size_law_verified_against_measurem: v0.27.1 vllm/platforms/interface.py computes attn_block_size = kernel_block_alignment_size * cdiv(mamba_page_size, kernel_block_alignment_size * attn_page_size_1_token), then 'if cache_config.block_size < attn_block_size: cache_config.block_size = attn_block_size'. With kernel_block_alignment_size = max(min supported kernel block, requested block): requested 64 -> 64*cdiv(K,64)=1088 => K in (1040,1056]; requested 16 -> 16*cdiv(K,16)=1056 => K in (1040,1056]. Both measured resolutions (1088 and 1056) are reproduced by one single K (= mamba state bytes / per-token attention page bytes ~= 1041..1056 tokens), so the flag is NOT honoured as asked: it is a lower bound that the hybrid state page rounds UP.

quant_advice.verdict: NVFP4 (modelopt_fp4) IS supported for Qwen3.5 on v0.27.1, including the dense hybrid path; pass --quantization modelopt_fp4 (or omit -- vLLM auto-maps NVFP4 checkpoints to it). It does NOT change the prefix-cache hit fraction, so it is not a lever for the 0.869 cell.
quant_advice.pass_flag: --quantization modelopt_fp4 (equivalently: leave --quantization unset and let config.json quantization.quant_algo=NVFP4 resolve it).
quant_advice.supported_list_quote: docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md: "- `NVFP4`: ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints (use `quantization="modelopt_fp4"`)." and "For NVFP4 checkpoints, vLLM selects a GEMM kernel automatically at load time from the backends available on the current platform (CUTLASS, FlashInfer, Marlin, and others). On GPUs without a supported native FP4 GEMM kernel, vLLM falls back to weight-only (W4A16) execution via Marlin and logs a warning; this may reduce throughput for compute-heavy workloads."

quant_advice.cache_side_warning: Do NOT switch --kv-cache-dtype to nvfp4 to chase NVFP4: per-token attention page shrinks, so attn_block_size = align*cdiv(mamba_page, align*attn_page_per_token) roughly DOUBLES (1088 -> ~2176), i.e. a coarser reuse grid. Kv cache dtype 'nvfp4' exists in 0.27.1 (CacheConfig.CacheDType) and is rejected only with MLA (vllm/config/vllm.py validate_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_mla).

options.recommended: 64 (only together with --block-size 64, which resolves to 1088; 1088 = 2^6*17 so 16/32/64/68/136/272/544/1088 all divide it)
options.why: On a hybrid model the default matching unit is only as fine as the resolved physical block: hash_block_size = prefix_match_unit if set else gcd(group block sizes) = 1088. Setting it finer is what activates the mamba partial-tail machinery at all (scheduler: mamba_partial_cache_hit = need_mamba_block_aligned_split and hash_block_size < block_size), and it is that path that registers a state entry at the prompt's last hash boundary instead of only at a full-block boundary.
options.quote: "hash_block_size is the granularity at which Request.block_hashes is computed. Single group: equals scheduler block size. Multiple groups: cache_config.prefix_match_unit override if set, else the GCD of group block sizes; every group's block size must be divisible by it. ... Returns the scheduler block size (i.e. disables finer hashing) if ... a mamba group's block size diverges from the cache block size (mamba_cache_mode != "align")." / "raise ValueError(f"Invalid prefix_match_unit={hash_block_size}; all KV cache group block sizes must be divisible by prefix_match_unit. Got group block sizes={group_block_sizes}.")" ; scheduler quote: "# A finer prefix_match_unit is configured: a mamba partial tail entry can only be registered by a step ending exactly at the prompt's last hash boundary, so the split adds that stop.  self.mamba_partial_cache_hit = (self.need_mamba_block_aligned_split and self.hash_block_size < self.block_size)"
options.expected_effect: Cuts the always-lost tail of each turn from a ~1088-token floor to a 64-token floor (plus the turn's own new tokens). Hypothesis ~0.86-0.90 tokens/turn recovery region; NOT measured here -- verify by rerunning the identical 32k/71-turn battery and reading cached_tokens per turn.

options.recommended: explicit 64 if you want a 64-token grid (1088 % 64 == 0); explicit 16 only if you want the finest possible grid (1056 % 64 != 0, so 1056 forbids --prefix-match-unit 64; 32 is the finest clean divisor there)
options.why: The requested value is a LOWER BOUND, never a setting: for hybrid mamba/attention models vLLM raises it until the attention page is at least the mamba state page. The resolved value is therefore a property of the model's hybrid state size, not of the flag -- which is exactly why 64 gave 1088 and 16 gave 1056.
options.quote: "For hybrid attention/mamba models, ensure that the attention page size is >= the mamba page size, and pad the mamba page size to match." / "attn_block_size = kernel_block_alignment_size * cdiv(mamba_page_size, kernel_block_alignment_size * attn_page_size_1_token)" / "if cache_config.block_size < attn_block_size: cache_config.block_size = attn_block_size" / logger.info("Setting attention block size to %d tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.") / "if cache_config.mamba_cache_mode == "align": cache_config.mamba_block_size = cache_config.block_size"
options.expected_effect: Explains the 1088/1056 pair exactly (single implied mamba-page ratio K ~= 1041..1056 tokens, i.e. mamba state ~= 17.0-17.3 MB at 16384 B/token of fp8 KV for 8 full-attention layers). Making the choice explicit stops the grid from drifting with model/state-dtype changes.

top3.why: Only this makes the effective reuse unit finer than the 1088-token physical block, and it is the switch that turns on the mamba partial-tail entry at the prompt's last hash boundary (scheduler.py mamba_partial_cache_hit). Everything else in the flag list is a guard or a capacity knob.

top3.change: State --mamba-cache-mode align explicitly, and read the two startup lines ('Mamba cache mode is set to ...', 'Setting attention block size to %d tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.') to confirm what the engine actually chose.
top3.why: The auto-resolver already lands on align for Qwen3.5 (it raises on 'all'), so this is cheap insurance plus the only way to know the resolved block/mode that produced 1088 vs 1056.

top3.change: If you want the finest grid rather than SGLang-parity: --block-size 16 (resolves 1056) with --prefix-match-unit 32 (1056 = 2^5*3*11; 64 does not divide it).
top3.why: 1056 is the finest resolved block the hybrid state page permits at 16-token requests; 32 is its finest clean divisor above the default. Choosing 64/1088 instead is the apples-to-apples arm against the SGLang 64-token grid.

hit_fraction_explanation.best_explanation: Not 'the model is dense/smaller'. On a hybrid model the per-turn bill is set by the *state checkpoint boundary*, and 0.27.1 only materialises a mamba state at a chunk end that is block-aligned, plus (only when hash_block_size < block_size) one extra stop at the prompt's last hash boundary. With --prefix-match-unit unset, hash_block_size = gcd(group block sizes) = the resolved block, so the 9B's reuse quantum was its full 1088 tokens (measured loss 2230.8/turn = 2.05 blocks) while the MoE's 2096-token resolve did not translate into a 2096-token loss (1682.7/turn = 0.80 blocks). Those two ratios cannot both be explained by the scheduler block alone, which falsifies the naive 'one block per turn' law and points at the effective hash unit: on a model whose mamba block equals the cache block the quantum is the whole block, and on a coarser-resolved model it evidently was not. So the answer is granularity-of-state, not parameter density.
hit_fraction_explanation.falsification_arithmetic: 2230.8 / 1088 = 2.05 blocks; 1682.7 / 2096 = 0.80 blocks. A single block-quantised law predicts both models lose >= 1 block per turn; the MoE clearly did not. Therefore the 0.869 cell is a *state-checkpoint granularity* artefact, not a 'dense model' artefact.
documented_terms_that_can_produce_the_ga: hash_block_size = prefix_match_unit else gcd(group block sizes) (kv_cache_utils.py:678-687) -- the number that actually floors each hit.

align-mode stop rule: 'Only cache the mamba state of the last token of each scheduler step and when the token is at position i * block_size' (cache.py mamba_cache_mode docstring) + last_cache_position = num_tokens - num_tokens % block_size (scheduler.py).
mamba_partial_cache_hit only exists when hash_block_size < block_size, i.e. only if you pass --prefix-match-unit (scheduler.py:317-321).
chunk-end alignment: 'State is written at chunk ends, so chunk ends must be block aligned' (scheduler.py) -- a chunk budget below the resolved block silently drops cacheable positions.
hit_fraction_explanation.decisive_diagnostic_instead_of_more_gues: Read from each engine's resolved config / startup log: block_size, mamba_block_size, mamba_cache_mode, hash_block_size, attn_tokens_per_mamba_state. This unit had no GX10 access (read-only, 0 live requests), so the sign of the gap cannot be closed from source alone.
hit_fraction_explanation.side_note_on_vram: Dense-vs-MoE also differ in whether the mamba state page is the binding term: resolved block = align*cdiv(mamba_page, align*attn_page_per_token). The 9B's implied ratio is ~1041-1056 tokens of attention KV per mamba state page (~17.0-17.3 MB); a model with a bigger state page per unit of KV gets a coarser block, not a better cache.

prompt_layout_guidance.mechanism: Hashes are chained over the whole prefix, and only full blocks are cached, so reuse requires a byte-stable token prefix: any edit, reordering, timestamp, per-request nonce or tool-list change ahead of the changed text invalidates every block after it.
quotes: docs/design/prefix_caching.md: "we hash each kv-cache block by the tokens in the block and the tokens in the prefix before the block" ... "Parent hash value: The hash value of the parent hash block." ... "!!! note "Note 1" We only cache full blocks."

docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md: "!!! warning  Claude Code recently started injecting a per-request hash in the system prompt, which can defeat prefix caching because the prompt changes on every request, causing greatly reduced performance. This is addressed automatically in vLLM versions > 0.17.1 but for older versions "CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER": "0" should be added to the "env" section of ~/.claude/settings.json"

docs/design/prefix_caching.md (cache_salt): "By including a cache_salt in the request, this value is injected into the hash of the first block ... With this setup, cache sharing is limited to users or requests that explicitly agree on a common salt"
actionable: Keep the system prompt byte-identical across turns and pin it first; never inject timestamps, request ids, abbreviated hashes or rotating tool lists into it.
Append-only conversation: tool results must be appended, never rewritten/reordered/summarised in place mid-context.
Do not vary cache_salt (or per-request 'extra_hashes' inputs) between turns of one agentic episode.
Fill the tail (the last partial block) with content that is not expected to survive the next turn; put durable context early so it lands on full-block boundaries.

next_unit_hint: A GX10-side unit should read the two startup log lines ('Setting attention block size to %d tokens ...' and 'Mamba cache mode is set to ...') from the already-recorded 1088 and 1056 runs, then run one arm with --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align on the same 32k/71-turn battery and diff cached_tokens per turn.
